cohort: Premature newborns with mild-to-moderate Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) receiving surfactant via tracheal catheterization while on non-invasive Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP).
finding: Less invasive surfactant instillation via tracheal catheterization was effective in 79.2% of premature newborns with RDS, with catheterization being 100% successful; factors associated with treatment failure included pH <= 7.20 and lack of lung maturation.
